content.json:
# CAMS Executive Usage Overview

Consolidated stakeholder view of growth, engagement, feature adoption, and reliability. Built entirely from existing Application Insights telemetry (pageViews, customEvents) plus the auto-generated anonymous per-browser `user_Id` — no new instrumentation required.

**Known approximations:** engagement is per-browser (not per-person) since real authenticated user identity is not wired into telemetry today; Case Notes usage is a tab-visit proxy, not confirmed note creation; Data Verification cannot be broken out by order type (Transfer/Consolidation/Trustee Mismatch) since all three share one URL.

## Growth & Engagement

Engagement is measured against App Insights' auto-generated anonymous `user_Id` (one per browser), not real authenticated identity.

**Growth Summary** gives three top-line numbers for the selected time range: how many distinct browsers were active, how many showed up for the first time, and how that compares to the prior 30-day period (month-over-month growth).

content.title: Growth Summary

content.json: **DAU / WAU / MAU** count distinct active browsers per day, over a rolling 7-day window, and over a rolling 30-day window. **Stickiness** (DAU÷MAU) is a standard engagement measure — the higher it is, the more the monthly total is made up of people who show up daily rather than just once a month.

content.query:
let raw = union pageViews, customEvents | where timestamp > ago(120d) | project timestamp, user_Id;
let dau = raw
    | summarize DAU = dcount(user_Id) by Day = bin(timestamp, 1d);
let wau = raw
    | extend Day = bin(timestamp, 1d)
    | mv-expand WindowDay = range(Day, Day + 6d, 1d) to typeof(datetime)
    | summarize WAU = dcount(user_Id) by Day = WindowDay;
let mau = raw
    | extend Day = bin(timestamp, 1d)
    | mv-expand WindowDay = range(Day, Day + 29d, 1d) to typeof(datetime)
    | summarize MAU = dcount(user_Id) by Day = WindowDay;
dau
| join kind=fullouter wau on Day
| join kind=fullouter mau on Day
| project Day = coalesce(Day, Day1, Day2), DAU = coalesce(DAU, 0), WAU = coalesce(WAU, 0), MAU = coalesce(MAU, 0)
| extend Stickiness = round(iif(MAU > 0, 100.0 * DAU / MAU, 0.0), 1)
| where Day > ago(90d) and Day <= bin(now(), 1d)
| order by Day asc
content.title: DAU / WAU / MAU and Stickiness (DAU÷MAU %)

content.json: **Engaged vs. Occasional Users** splits browsers by how many distinct days they were active in the period: 8+ days is "Engaged," fewer is "Occasional" (that 8-day line is provisional — see the open ticket item to tune it against real traffic). **New vs. Returning Users** splits browsers by whether their very first-ever visit falls inside the selected period ("New") or happened earlier ("Returning").

content.query:
union pageViews, customEvents
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| summarize ActiveDays = dcount(startofday(timestamp)) by user_Id
| extend Segment = iif(ActiveDays >= 8, "Engaged (8+ active days)", "Occasional (1-7 active days)")
| summarize Users = count() by Segment
content.title: Engaged vs. Occasional Users

content.query:
let FirstSeen = union pageViews, customEvents | where timestamp > ago(400d) | summarize FirstSeen = min(timestamp) by user_Id;
union pageViews, customEvents
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| summarize by user_Id
| join kind=inner FirstSeen on user_Id
| extend Status = iif(FirstSeen >= {TimeRange:start} and FirstSeen <= {TimeRange:end}, "New", "Returning")
| summarize Users = count() by Status
content.title: New vs. Returning Users

content.json: **Weekly Cohort Retention** groups users by the week they first showed up (their "cohort"), then tracks what percentage of that same group is still active in each week afterward. Each line is one starting week; a line that drops fast means those users didn't stick around, a line that stays high means they kept coming back. Because it takes a few weeks to build up a retention curve, only cohorts old enough to have that history are shown.

content.query:
let raw = union pageViews, customEvents | where timestamp > ago(120d) | project timestamp, user_Id;
let cohorts = raw | summarize CohortWeek = startofweek(min(timestamp)) by user_Id;
let cohortSizes = cohorts | summarize CohortSize = count() by CohortWeek;
raw
| extend ActiveWeek = startofweek(timestamp)
| join kind=inner cohorts on user_Id
| extend WeekNumber = datetime_diff('week', ActiveWeek, CohortWeek)
| where WeekNumber >= 0 and WeekNumber <= 8
| where CohortWeek > ago(70d)
| summarize ActiveUsers = dcount(user_Id) by CohortWeek, WeekNumber
| join kind=inner cohortSizes on CohortWeek
| extend RetentionPercent = round(100.0 * ActiveUsers / CohortSize, 1)
| project CohortWeek = format_datetime(CohortWeek, 'yyyy-MM-dd'), WeekNumber, RetentionPercent
| order by CohortWeek asc, WeekNumber asc
content.title: Weekly Cohort Retention (% of cohort still active by week N)

content.json:
## Feature Adoption

Every case-detail and trustee-detail tab is a distinct route, and the app already auto-tracks a `pageView` on every route change — so this is a direct measure of which tabs are actually being visited, no new instrumentation needed. **Data Verification** is a single URL (its three order types render as accordions, not routes) so it cannot be broken out further without new instrumentation.
**Tab-Level Adoption** ranks every tab and section by what percentage of all active users visited it at least once during the period — a snapshot of which features get used at all.

content.query:
let Routes = pageViews
    | where timestamp {TimeRange}
    | where isnotempty(url)
    | extend Section = case(
        url contains "/case-detail/" or url contains "/my-cases" or (url contains "/search" and not(url contains "/case-detail/")), "Cases",
        url contains "/trustees", "Trustees",
        url contains "/data-verification", "Data Verification",
        url contains "/staff-assignment", "Staff Assignment",
        "Other"
      )
    | extend Tab = case(
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/my-cases", "My Cases (list)",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/search" and not(url contains "/case-detail/"), "Case Search",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/trustee-and-assigned-staff", "Assigned Staff",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/court-docket", "Court Docket",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/notes", "Case Notes",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/associated-cases", "Associated Cases",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/audit-history", "Change History",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/trustee", "Trustee",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/case-detail/", "Overview",
        Section == "Trustees" and url endswith "/trustees", "Trustees List",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/appointments", "Appointments",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/assigned-staff", "Assigned Staff",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/audit-history", "Change History",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/notes", "Trustee Notes",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/cases", "Case List",
        Section == "Trustees", "Overview",
        Section == "Data Verification", "Data Verification",
        Section == "Staff Assignment", "Staff Assignment",
        "Other"
      )
    | where Section != "Other";
let TotalActiveUsers = toscalar(pageViews | where timestamp {TimeRange} | summarize dcount(user_Id));
Routes
| summarize UsersVisiting = dcount(user_Id) by Section, Tab
| extend ['% of Active Users'] = round(100.0 * UsersVisiting / TotalActiveUsers, 1)
| project Section, Tab, UsersVisiting, ['% of Active Users']
| order by Section asc, ['% of Active Users'] desc
content.title: Tab-Level Adoption (% of active users visiting each tab)

content.json: **Tab Adoption Trend** shows that same tab-visit metric broken out week by week instead of as one snapshot, so you can see whether adoption of a tab (or a whole section, via the filter below) is growing, flat, or shrinking over time.

content.query:
let Routes = pageViews
    | where timestamp {TimeRange}
    | where isnotempty(url)
    | extend Section = case(
        url contains "/case-detail/" or url contains "/my-cases" or (url contains "/search" and not(url contains "/case-detail/")), "Cases",
        url contains "/trustees", "Trustees",
        url contains "/data-verification", "Data Verification",
        url contains "/staff-assignment", "Staff Assignment",
        "Other"
      )
    | extend Tab = case(
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/my-cases", "My Cases (list)",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/search" and not(url contains "/case-detail/"), "Case Search",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/trustee-and-assigned-staff", "Assigned Staff",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/court-docket", "Court Docket",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/notes", "Case Notes",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/associated-cases", "Associated Cases",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/audit-history", "Change History",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/trustee", "Trustee",
        Section == "Cases" and url contains "/case-detail/", "Overview",
        Section == "Trustees" and url endswith "/trustees", "Trustees List",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/appointments", "Appointments",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/assigned-staff", "Assigned Staff",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/audit-history", "Change History",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/notes", "Trustee Notes",
        Section == "Trustees" and url contains "/cases", "Case List",
        Section == "Trustees", "Overview",
        Section == "Data Verification", "Data Verification",
        Section == "Staff Assignment", "Staff Assignment",
        "Other"
      )
    | where Section != "Other";
let TotalActiveUsers = toscalar(pageViews | where timestamp {TimeRange} | summarize dcount(user_Id));
Routes
| where '{SectionFilter}' == 'value::all' or Section == '{SectionFilter}'
| summarize UsersVisiting = dcount(user_Id) by Tab, Week = startofweek(timestamp)
| extend ['% of Active Users'] = round(100.0 * UsersVisiting / TotalActiveUsers, 1)
| order by Week asc
content.title: Tab Adoption Trend

content.json: **Search Click-Through Rate** approximates search success: of all searches performed, what percentage were followed by a click on a result within 5 minutes. There's no "zero results" signal in telemetry today, so this is the closest available proxy — a low rate could mean bad results, or just a user who found what they needed some other way.

content.query:
let SearchEvents = customEvents | where timestamp {TimeRange} | where name == "search" | project session_Id, SearchTime = timestamp;
let ClickEvents = customEvents | where timestamp {TimeRange} | where name == "searchResultClick" | project session_Id, ClickTime = timestamp;
SearchEvents
| join kind=leftouter ClickEvents on session_Id
| where isnull(ClickTime) or ClickTime >= SearchTime
| summarize HadClick = max(isnotempty(ClickTime) and (ClickTime - SearchTime) < 5m) by session_Id, SearchTime
| summarize TotalSearches = count(), SearchesWithClick = countif(HadClick)
| extend ['Click-Through Rate %'] = round(iif(TotalSearches > 0, 100.0 * SearchesWithClick / TotalSearches, 0.0), 1)
| project TotalSearches, SearchesWithClick, ['Click-Through Rate %']
content.title: Search Click-Through Rate (proxy for search success — no zero-result field exists in telemetry today)

content.json:
### Notes Engagement

Called out specifically since stakeholders have asked about these two features. **Trustee Notes Engagement** is pulled directly from the existing nightly Trustee Notes aggregate: what percentage of trustees have at least one note, what percentage of users have engaged with notes, and how many notes were created in the last 24 hours. **Case Notes Visit Rate** is a rougher proxy — no equivalent backend aggregate exists yet for Case Notes, so this only measures what percentage of users who opened a case detail page also clicked into its Notes tab, not whether they actually wrote anything.

content.query:
app('{DataflowsAppInsights:name}').customEvents
| where customDimensions.moduleName == "SYNC-TRUSTEE-NOTES-METRICS"
| where name == "DataflowHandlerComplete"
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| extend
    TrusteesWithNotesPercent = todouble(customDimensions.trusteesWithNotesPercent),
    UserEngagementPercent = todouble(customDimensions.userEngagementPercent),
    NotesLast24Hrs = todouble(customDimensions.notesLast24Hrs)
| summarize
    ['Trustees With Notes %'] = round(max(TrusteesWithNotesPercent), 1),
    ['User Engagement %'] = round(max(UserEngagementPercent), 1),
    ['Notes Created (last 24h)'] = round(max(NotesLast24Hrs), 0)
    by Day = startofday(timestamp)
| order by Day asc
content.title: Trustee Notes Engagement (from existing SYNC-TRUSTEE-NOTES-METRICS aggregate)
Case Notes Visit Rate (proxy — tab visits, not confirmed note creation; no backend aggregate exists yet)

content.json:
## Reliability & Data Quality

System health, framed as the trust signal behind the usage numbers above.

**Page Load** and **Search Latency** show the P50 (typical) and P95 (worst-case-for-most-users) response times in milliseconds, day by day — a proxy for whether the app feels fast or sluggish to users.

content.query:
pageViews
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| summarize P50Ms = percentile(duration, 50), P95Ms = percentile(duration, 95) by Day = bin(timestamp, 1d)
| order by Day asc
content.title: Page Load Latency (P50 / P95, ms)

content.query:
customEvents
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| where name == "Case Search Performance"
| extend DurationMs = todouble(customMeasurements.durationMs)
| summarize P50Ms = percentile(DurationMs, 50), P95Ms = percentile(DurationMs, 95) by Day = bin(timestamp, 1d)
| order by Day asc
content.title: Search Latency (P50 / P95, ms)

content.json: **Frontend Exception Rate** normalizes JavaScript errors against traffic volume (errors per 1,000 page views) so a spike isn't just an artifact of more people using the app. **Dataflow Sync Success Rate** tracks the health of the backend jobs that keep CAMS data in sync — a drop here means the numbers elsewhere in this workbook (and in the app itself) may be stale.

content.query:
let dailyExceptions = exceptions | where timestamp {TimeRange} | summarize Exceptions = count() by Day = bin(timestamp, 1d);
let dailyViews = pageViews | where timestamp {TimeRange} | summarize Views = count() by Day = bin(timestamp, 1d);
dailyViews
| join kind=fullouter dailyExceptions on Day
| project Day = coalesce(Day, Day1), Exceptions = coalesce(Exceptions, 0), Views = coalesce(Views, 0)
| extend ['Exceptions per 1,000 Views'] = round(iif(Views > 0, 1000.0 * Exceptions / Views, 0.0), 2)
| order by Day asc
content.title: Frontend Exception Rate

content.query:
app('{DataflowsAppInsights:name}').customEvents
| where timestamp {TimeRange}
| where name == "DataflowHandlerComplete"
| extend Success = tostring(customDimensions.success)
| summarize Total = count(), Succeeded = countif(Success == "true") by Day = bin(timestamp, 1d)
| extend ['Success Rate %'] = round(iif(Total > 0, 100.0 * Succeeded / Total, 0.0), 1)
| order by Day asc
content.title: Dataflow Sync Success Rate (data freshness health)
